title: Hive Mind Inbox Entry Frontmatter
description: Required frontmatter on every `_inbox/*.md` contribution. Parliament Sentinel rejects files whose frontmatter fails this schema before any other processing.
$comment: Parliament Step 2.0 (Frontmatter Normalizer, see protocol/custodian-workflow.md) recognizes common alt-field aliases and adds canonical fields alongside before validation. Aliases: contributor/contributed_by -> author; session_date -> date; type:<value> -> tag:<canonical-value>. The normalizer is additive only — it never deletes or overwrites fields the author wrote. Contributors should still write canonical fields by default; assets/inbox-template.md is the reference shape.

author.description: GitHub username or verifiable identity of the contributor. Must match commit author for attribution chain integrity.

date.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) the contribution was drafted.

tag.description: Contribution category — determines triage path (fast vs. deliberation). See `protocol/triage-policy.md`.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Only `ready` files are picked up by Parliament. `active` = session still in progress; `completed` = Parliament has processed.

target_file.description: Optional hint from the author for which knowledge file this contribution updates. Archivist may override.

source.description: Optional citation (URL, file path, meeting reference, Slack message timestamp). Strongly encouraged for `[status]`, `[correction]`, `[contradiction]`.

session_id.description: Optional Claude Code session identifier for attribution chain.

sentinel_override.description: Audit record of a user-approved override of pre-push Sentinel pattern match(es). Recorded by the session agent during the pre-push scan after explicit user approval. Parliament Sentinel reads this field and skips quarantine for the listed pattern names while still scanning for new patterns. See `protocol/sensitive-data-patterns.md` § Override audit trail.

reviewed_by.description: Git user (from `git config user.name`) who approved the override.

reviewed_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the override was recorded.

patterns.description: Pattern names from `protocol/sensitive-data-patterns.md` that were overridden. Each name corresponds to a row in the Credentials or PII tables.

justification.description: Brief reason supplied by the user explaining why the match is a false positive.

matches.description: Recommended. The matched line excerpts (as reported by the hook) this override covers. When present, the override is excerpt-bound: it suppresses a listed pattern only on lines containing one of these strings, so editing the matched line or a new match elsewhere blocks again. Omitting it keeps the legacy per-file scope.
